data.name: Private Detective Punch Drunk
data.detailed_description:
Private Detective Punch Drunk is the only game to let you legally kick ass under the influence.

PDPD, is a 2.5D side scrolling beat 'em up where you must fight your way through a sinister video game corporation, hell bent on destroying our drinking money.

The corporation is determined to take successful gaming tropes and turn them into "In-Life" pay-to-win micro-transactions. They must be stopped with our drunken fists.

Fight your way through 10 familiar diverse levels to destroy the masterminds behind these evil ideas.

Compete for the high score worldwide with a fully integrated online scoreboard.

Can you defeat these monsters who seek to destroy the video game industry? Only you can save the video game industry we know and love.

reviews.review:
On paper, a noir-styled beat ’em up with sharp dialogue sounds like an interesting spin on the genre. In practice? *Private Detective Punch Drunk* is one of those games where the idea is better than the execution, and it shows with every second of playtime.  

[h2] GOOD [/h2]  
[list]  
[*][b] Noir Theme is a Solid Concept [/b]  
A pulp-inspired detective beat ’em up is a great hook. In another developer’s hands, this could’ve been stylish, atmospheric, and memorable. Sadly, here it’s wasted potential.  

[*][b] Effort in Dialogue [/b]  
The only aspect that feels like it had real attention put into it is the dialogue. It’s clear some work went into giving the game a “voice,” and while it doesn’t redeem the rest, it deserves credit.  
[/list]  

[h2] BAD [/h2]  
[list]  
[*][b] Awful Optimization & Gameplay [/b]  
The game is poorly optimized to the point of being a chore to play. Enemy design has no creativity, combat is bone-dry, and every encounter feels like you’ve seen it a dozen times before. “Boring” and “sloppy” are the best words to describe it.  

[*][b] Shallow Development [/b]  
The noir aesthetic and dialogue can’t hide the fact that this is hardly a finished product. No style can cover up uninspired beat ’em up mechanics that never evolve past button-mashing monotony.  

[*][b] Developer Abandonment [/b]  
Here’s the biggest red flag: the devs effectively cut and ran. Instead of patching or refining the game, they abandoned it to chase something else. That’s not just bad practice—it’s disrespectful to the people who actually supported it. This reeks of a quick cash grab rather than a genuine attempt at building a long-term title.  
[/list]  

[h2] FINAL THOUGHT [/h2]  
*Private Detective Punch Drunk* is a perfect example of wasted potential. Noir beat ’em up? Great idea. But poor optimization, lifeless combat, and an early-abandoned development cycle kill any hope the concept had.  

Here’s some advice for the devs: if you can’t build something polished for Steam, start smaller. Release your projects on Itch.io, gather actual feedback, and improve before charging people full price on a platform like this. Steam isn’t a proving ground for half-baked experiments—it’s a marketplace. Players deserve better.  

As it stands, this isn’t just a bad beat ’em up—it’s a cautionary tale. Skip it.
